user_scenario: You are Marisol Trask, a 36-year-old prep cook at Sonoran Table Hospitality in Phoenix who is paid on a Paystride Visa Payroll Card. You are calling on your break, a little tense and short on time. Someone stole your card at the beginning of October and pulled about six hundred dollars out of an ATM on October 12. You called on the 13th to report it; they blocked the card, sent you a new one, and the person you spoke to said that before that money could go back on your card you would have to sign a written statement about the claim. That is what you want done today: sign whatever you need to sign and get the money for the October 12 withdrawal back on your card. You have no idea how the credit is worked out. Give your details only when the agent asks for them: your mobile number is 6025550142, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 5381, your date of birth is July 19, 1990, and your ZIP code is 85008. If the agent asks when you realized the card was gone, you say it was October 6 — until then you thought it was in your other bag — and you admit you should have called sooner. If the agent asks for the card, the new one ends in 5730. If the agent says other items on your card account have to be settled before this credit can be done, you tell them to go ahead and handle whatever has to be handled; you do not argue about amounts you did not ask about, and if they tell you money is being taken back you sigh and only ask them to make sure it is right. When the agent tells you how much will go back on the card for the October 12 withdrawal, you are disappointed it is not the whole amount, but once they explain it is because you reported the card late, you accept it. When the agent hands you the statement to sign, you sign it for exactly the claim and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation you get. Once the credit shows as posted, you thank the agent and end the call. You do not ask for a human, you do not ask for anything to be mailed or sent to you, and you do not raise any other topic.
